item.title: Meta Launches AI Tools for Game Development on Horizon Platform
item.description:
Meta Launches AI Tools for Game Development on Horizon Platform

Meta has announced a plan to encourage game creation for its Horizon social platform through two new AI-powered development tools. This move follows a recent pivot for Horizon, which launched as a VR app but now primarily focuses on mobile.

🧩 How it works

Meta is introducing tools that allow users to create games using AI prompts. According to Meta, these tools enable creators to turn ideas into complete 2D or 3D mobile games that include:

  • Progression systems
  • Balanced difficulty
  • Art direction
  • Multiplayer

⚙️ Key details

Tool Platform Description
Horizon Create Mobile App Create games with AI prompts
Horizon Studio Browser App Create games with AI prompts and more granular controls

To increase the reach of these games, Meta will allow titles made with Horizon Create and Horizon Studio to be recommended and played directly on Facebook and Instagram. Meta states, “Someone scrolling through Instagram can tap a clip of your game and be in a multiplayer session within seconds, without needing to download an app or being redirected.” Games that are “engaging, stable, culturally relevant, and keep players coming back” will receive more reach.

🚀 Availability

The apps will be available in early access, and interested users can sign up for a waitlist.

💡 Why it matters

This push into AI-generated video games comes as Roblox, a similar and more popular platform with 123 million daily active users, is also implementing AI-powered development features in its mobile app. By contrast, Horizon has struggled to gain similar scale, with a 2022 report indicating it had 300,000 monthly users.

#Meta #Horizon #AI #GameDev

Source: Meta is going to let you build games with AI right on your phone

item.title: NVIDIA Updates DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering
item.description:
NVIDIA Updates DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering

NVIDIA has updated DLSS 5 to introduce DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, providing game developers with granular controls to add material detail and lifelike lighting while preserving artistic intent.

🧩 How it works

DLSS 5 extends the graphics pipeline by adding a final neural-rendering stage. This process uses the following as an unyielding foundation:

  • The game engine’s rendered frame
  • Artist-authored geometry
  • Textures
  • Lighting buffers

⚙️ Key details

Developers have access to several tools to tune the output:

  • Model Selection: Developers can choose from multiple models and mix them across scenes, gameplay, or cutscenes.
  • Tuning Controls: Structure Intensity and Tone Intensity can be adjusted to tune broader lighting, color response, and high-frequency detail.
  • Masking: Semantic AI masking can apply or hold back effects across recognized scene elements, while engine-level masks can isolate asset groups such as foliage, water droplets, or glassware.

🚀 Availability

DLSS 5 runs locally on a single GeForce RTX 50 Series GPU at up to 4K. It is currently available via:

  • Hardware: All GeForce RTX 50 Series desktop and laptop GPUs.
  • Games: NBA 2K27, developed by Visual Concepts and published by 2K.
  • Cloud: GeForce NOW Ultimate members streaming from NVIDIA-operated GeForce RTX 5080-powered gaming rigs.

💡 Why it matters

In the case of NBA 2K27, DLSS 5 preserves scanned facial geometry while enhancing the following:

  • Skin subsurface scattering
  • Contact shadows
  • Light transmission through ears and hair

#NVIDIA #DLSS #NeuralRendering #GeForceRTX #GameDev

Source: What’s New for Game Developers: DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, NVIDIA ACE Updates, and New RTX Kit Capabilities | NVIDIA Technical Blog
